result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens does `const response = await fetch(...); return response;` with no status/ok check, and call sites (e.g. googlecalendar CalendarService) immediately treat the result as a token response (`token.access_token`, `token.expiry_date`). A non-2xx or HTML error body from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT would be parsed as success and produce undefined/NaN tokens with no diagnostic context. Verifiable directly from the new file in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns the raw `fetch()` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` without checking `response.ok`/status or parsing the body. Several call sites assume a successful, already-parsed token object/shape (e.g. `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` does `const token = res?.data;` then reads `token.access_token`, and `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` types the return as `HubspotToken`, and Zoho uses `tokenInfo.data`). If the sync endpoint returns 4xx/5xx or non-JSON/HTML, this will not be detected at the helper boundary and will fail later with misleading errors, and no contextual info (appSlug/userId) is attached.
